newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL STOCKS END LOWER, SEEN VOLATILE NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL STOCKS END LOWER, SEEN VOLATILE NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Brazil shares closed 1.57 percent lower in thin volume Friday, with analysts expecting volatility next week as the expiraton dates of mid-August futures index and options approach.
"Next week the bolsa may see some volatility ahead of the options and futures settlements," a senior trader added.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 47 most active stocks ended off 195 points at 12,128 points. Total market turnover was a lighter-than-average 547.4 million reais ($506.8 million).
Volume of the shares that make up the Bovespa index totaled 450.9 million reais ($417.5 million).

Traders virtually shrugged off the awarding of two more Band B cellular telephone concessions on Friday, as well as a legal challenge that could result in the overturning of one of those awards next week.
The Communications Ministry announced that a group including Sweden's Telia won bidding on a concession to operate cellular services in an area covering non-metropolitan Sao Paulo state.
But Brazil's Supreme Tribunal of Justice next week may still disqualify the group, which had obtained an injunction allowing it to compete.
In addition, a consortium that includes BellSouth Corp of the United States was awarded a contract to operate cellular services in six northeastern states.
Telia group offered 1.326 billion reais for its concession, while BellSouth's bid was 555.6 million reais.
Traders said the results had already been factored into share prices, even though the winning bid for Brazil's northeast was well above market expectations.
"There was not much excitement about the opening of those bids," one said.
Analysts said losses on Wall Street contributed to weakness in Brazilian stocks, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 156.78 points, or 1.91 percent, to 8031.22.
Among leading Brazilian shares, benchmark Telebras preferred closed off 2.15 percent at 149.70 reais. Federal power utility Eletrobras ended off 1.47 percent at 600.01 reais.
State oil company Petrobras preferred lost 0.98 percent to 302 reais.
Preferred shares of CVRD, the recently privatized mining group, dropped 1.06 percent at 27.80 reais.
Brazilian shares dropped one percent during the week, bringing their losses for the month so far to 5.7 percent. Still, the bolsa has gained 72.2 percent in the year to date.
